Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment summary from transcript:
  - Acute left-sided headache waking patient from sleep (~05:30 today), persistent since onset. Described as severe; mild photophobia (light makes eyes sore). Transient dizziness on waking that resolved. No nausea/vomiting, no fever, no neck stiffness. Paracetamol taken with little benefit. Patient has 2-year history of anxiety on sertraline. Recent increased work stress and sleep deprivation (late nights ~2 months).
  - No vitals or physical examination recorded.
- Diagnostic reasoning (integrating DDx where consistent):
  - Tension-type headache — high likelihood: consistent with history of prolonged work stress, anxiety, late nights; clinician also identified this as a likely cause.
  - Migraine — moderate likelihood: unilateral pain and photophobia fit migraine features; triggers (stress, sleep disturbance) present.
  - Headache related to sleep deprivation/dehydration — moderate likelihood: recent late nights and possible inadequate hydration are plausible precipitants and were specifically advised to be addressed by clinician.
  - More serious secondary causes (e.g., subarachnoid hemorrhage) were considered in DDx as low-likelihood differentials given acute waking headache; transcript lacks red-flag features (no neck stiffness, vomiting, focal deficits). No direct evidence in transcript to support these; not included in top 3. (No conflict between transcript and DDx; DDx appropriately raised low-likelihood serious causes for safety.)
- Contradictions/uncertain items: No direct contradictions between transcript and DDx; DDx expands differential to include less likely but serious causes which are not supported by exam or red flags in transcript.

- Primary immediate management (from transcript):
  - Recommend starting ibuprofen for presumed migraine/tension-type headache — dose/route/frequency not documented. Paracetamol may be continued (patient already took paracetamol; dose not documented).  
  - Self-certify time off work (suggestion of ~1 week) to reduce stress and facilitate recovery.  
  - Referral / self-referral to local counselling service (link to be provided in notes) for ongoing stress/anxiety management.  
  - Lifestyle advice: Aim for 7–8 hours sleep nightly; drink 1.5–2 L fluids per day (excluding coffee/tea); avoid dehydration and fatigue.  
  - Safety-netting: Follow-up arranged in 1 week (with same clinician or another GP). If symptoms worsen or new features develop (worsening pain, fever, neck stiffness, vomiting, focal neurological signs, collapse), contact clinic urgently or present for reassessment.  
  - If no improvement at follow-up, consider blood tests and/or further investigations/imaging (not yet ordered in this consultation).
- Other items documented/discussed:
